claims.basis: FIA homologation and period competition references identify the Mk I RS1600 and its Group 2 context; the local observation identifies the exact simulator package.

The FIA form specifies synchronized forward ratios and the period competition reference excludes dog engagement for the relevant configuration. The homologation describes a manual remote floor control; the competition references describe manual gearboxes, not sequential or paddle actuation. The manual H-pattern arrangement requires a clutch to pull away from rest under the project's derivation rules. Established synchromesh construction settles ordinary running-shift clutch technique as required. Manual blip is a downshift action and is not applicable to the upshift field. Automatic blip is a downshift action and is not applicable to the upshift field. Synchromesh construction settles ordinary running-shift clutch technique as required. Throttle lift is modeled only for upshifts in this schema. Automatic cut is modeled only for upshifts in this schema. The project's synchromesh derivation records a downshift blip as optional. The period manual competition gearbox sources describe no electronic automatic-blip system. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/forward_gears, /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_pattern, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shape, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/integrated_display, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/open_top.
